'''Dorje C. Brody''' (born 1970 in Hong Kong) is a British [[Applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]].

== Career ==
Dorje C. Brody was born in [[Hong Kong]], but lived in Japan for a number of years. He received his BSc in physics at [[Niigata University]] and earned an MSc and PhD degrees in [[theoretical physics]] from [[Imperial College London|Imperial]].

Brody held a [[PPARC]] (Particle Physics and Astronomy Research Council) research fellowship in the [[Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] in [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]], in conjunction with a Research Fellowship at [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]]. In 1999 he returned to Imperial College as a [[Royal Society]] University Research Fellow. In 2004 Brody was invited to the Imperial Palace in Tokyo as an Outstanding Young Person to meet the Emperor of Japan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://toyp.osaka-jc.or.jp/TOYP2015Report.pdf|title=The Outstanding Young Persons Report 2015|website=Junior Chamber International Osaka (Japan)}}</ref>  Brody has been a full professor since 2011 and since 2018 he has held a Chair in Mathematics at the University of Surrey in the UK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.surrey.ac.uk/people/dorje-brody|title=Dorje C Brody {{!}} University of Surrey|website=www.surrey.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-05-26}}</ref>

Brody's research covers a broad range of topics in applied mathematics and theoretical physics.  During the early part of his career he focused on statistical mechanics, which led naturally to stochastic processes and financial mathematics in one direction and to thermodynamics and quantum mechanics in another.  Brody's work has covered [[information geometry]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C|last2=Hook|first2=Daniel W|title=Information geometry in vapour–liquid equilibrium|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=42|issue=2|article-number=023001|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/42/2/023001|year=2009|arxiv=0809.1166|bibcode=2009JPhA...42b3001B|s2cid=118311636}}</ref> and geometric quantum theory<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Hughston|first2=Lane P.|title=Geometric quantum mechanics|journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics|volume=38|issue=1|pages=19–53|doi=10.1016/s0393-0440(00)00052-8|year=2001|arxiv=quant-ph/9906086|bibcode=2001JGP....38...19B|s2cid=17580350}}</ref> as well as foundational issues in quantum theory, quantum statistical mechanics<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bender|first1=Carl M.|last2=Brody|first2=Dorje C.|last3=Meister|first3=Bernhard K.|date=2000|title=Quantum mechanical Carnot engine|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General|volume=33|issue=24|page=4427|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/33/24/302|issn=0305-4470|arxiv=quant-ph/0007002|bibcode=2000JPhA...33.4427B|s2cid=5335}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C|last2=Hughston|first2=Lane P|date=2016|title=Thermodynamics of quantum heat bath|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=49|issue=42|article-number=425302|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/49/42/425302|issn=1751-8113|arxiv=1406.5780|bibcode=2016JPhA...49.5302B|s2cid=53380629}}</ref> and quantum cosmology<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Hughston|first2=Lane P.|date=2005|title=Theory of quantum space-time|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences|volume=461|issue=2061|pages=2679–2699|doi=10.1098/rspa.2005.1457|issn=1364-5021|arxiv=gr-qc/0406121|bibcode=2005RSPSA.461.2679B|s2cid=18502302}}</ref> in theoretical physics; and using concepts of [[information geometry]], nonlinear filtering and [[information asymmetry]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Meister|first2=Bernhard K.|last3=Parry|first3=Matthew F.|date=2012|title=Informational inefficiency in financial markets|journal=Mathematics and Financial Economics|language=en|volume=6|issue=3|pages=249–259|doi=10.1007/s11579-012-0078-1|s2cid=154143369|issn=1862-9679}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Friedman|first2=Robyn L.|title=Information of Interest|journal=Risk Magazine |date=December 2009|pages=105–110|arxiv=0905.0072|bibcode=2009arXiv0905.0072B}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Hughston|first2=Lane P.|date=2001|title=Interest rates and information geometry|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences|volume=457|issue=2010|pages=1343–1363|doi=10.1098/rspa.2000.0722|issn=1364-5021|arxiv=1111.3757|bibcode=2001RSPSA.457.1343B|s2cid=123528394}}</ref> in financial mathematics. He is a member of the editorial boards of ''[[Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical]]'', ''[[International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance]]'' and ''[[Information Geometry (journal)|Information Geometry]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/d.brody|title=Home - Professor Dorje Brody|website=www.imperial.ac.uk|access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/mathematics/geometry/journal/41884?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Information Geometry (Editorial Board)|website=springer.com|language=en|access-date=2018-09-16}}</ref>

Brody has published more than 100 papers<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9242-9554|title=Dorje Brody (0000-0002-9242-9554) - ORCID|last=ORCID|website=orcid.org|access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://app.dimensions.ai/discover/publication?and_facet_researcher=ur.012050206755.23|title=Researcher (beta): Dorje C Brody in Publications - Dimensions|website=app.dimensions.ai|access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref> with his most recognisable contributions being in the complex extension of quantum mechanics known as [[Non-Hermitian quantum mechanics|PT-symmetric quantum mechanics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bender|first1=Carl M.|last2=Brody|first2=Dorje C.|last3=Jones|first3=Hugh F.|date=2002|title=Complex Extension of Quantum Mechanics|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=89|issue=27|article-number=270401|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.270401|pmid=12513185|arxiv=quant-ph/0208076|bibcode=2002PhRvL..89A0401B|s2cid=11004734}}</ref> and in the introduction of information-based asset pricing theory.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Financial Informatics: An Information-Based Approach to Asset Pricing|last1=Brody|first1=Dorje C.|last2=Hughston|first2=Lane P.|last3=Macrina|first3=Andrea|date=2022|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-12-4648-7}}</ref> Recently, his work (with [[Carl M. Bender]] and Markus Müller) on the [[Hilbert–Pólya conjecture]] received significant attention.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.altmetric.com/details/18294626|title=Altmetric – Hamiltonian for the
